evidence: STRUCTURE SUPPORTS A GRADED REWARD. (1) task/tests/scoring.toml:1-11 matches the template: gates render/constraints = 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05; task/tests/tools/score.py is identical to the template (diff empty). score.py:57-59 computes reward = weighted mean when gates_passed and floors_passed, else 0.0, so the only cliffs are the two gates and functional <= 0.05. (2) Functional (scored/functional/judge.toml) has 43 binary criteria with weights 0.5-2.5, total 58.5 (computed with tomllib); the largest criteria (hro_stale_refused, hro_live_board, hro_candidate_private at 2.5) are each 4.3% of functional, 2.6% of reward; aggregation = weighted_mean (line 21). (3) Polish has 5 binary criteria, weights 3, 3, 2, 1.5, 2.5 (total 12); visual has 5 likert criteria, points = 5, weight 1.2 each, with anchors 1-5 (visual/judge.toml:17-90), giving fine gradation. (4) Precondition collapse is explicitly mitigated: functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures ... A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row ... When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own'; prompt.md:39 gives a fallback to Tomas's seeded conversation if hro_candidate_linked fails; prompt.md:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'. Polish prompt.md:12 and visual prompt.md:12 grade independently after the gate. (5) The floor cuts only near-empty apps: gate plus hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate and hro_add_email_rules (weight 2.0) gives functional 2.0/58.5 = 0.034 <= 0.05, so reward 0; an app needs > 2.925 weight (2-3 working rules) for credit. That is intended anti-farming, not binary collapse. Worked spread (design-level, not measured): a competent app with no live push loses hro_live_board 2.5, hro_msg_exchange 1.5, hro_unread_counts 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_seen 1.5 = 9.5 functional (F ~0.84) and hro_pol_live_board + hro_pol_live_thread = 6/12 polish; with V ~0.75 the reward is ~0.6*0.84 + 0.2*0.5 + 0.2*0.75 = 0.75; also dropping undo (hro_undo_restores 2, hro_undo_conflict 2, hro_undo_once 1, hro_undo_full 0.5) gives ~0.69; a basic board with roles and no conversations lands far lower. The rubric is designed to discriminate. WHY NOT PASS. (a) No measured spread exists: raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' says 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only artifacts are scripted golden observations (workspace.cjs, workspace.json, server.log; hashes re-verified), with no weak or mutated app and no configured judge run. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires separate hash-bound runtime records for reward discrimination and ordering before local clearance. (b) Unmeasured all-or-nothing path through workload: test.sh:224-226 'if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0; fi'. If the scored RewardKit suite fails or times out, the reward stays the plain zero written at the start, whatever the app's quality. The functional judge (timeout 9000, batched, 43 criteria across 14 protocols Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D, many independent contexts, captured-request replays and repeated 15-second live waits) plus polish 900 and visual 900 run with --max-concurrent-agent 1 (test.sh:207) within an 11100 s budget. If the configured judge cannot finish, every app, the golden included, collapses to 0; or, under the 'NOT EXERCISED -> binary0' rule (functional/prompt.md:53), late protocols (K, R, V, A, D) get 0 by protocol order rather than app quality, compressing or reordering the spread. Whether that happens is exactly the missing workload/discrimination measurement. test.sh and score.py are template-controlled and must not be edited for this. Run verdict NOT EXERCISED: no configured judge run exists for the golden or any partial-quality app.
counterexample: Not a demonstrated defect; these are hypothetical risks to measure. Broken app that could still rank like a good one: none found structurally. A gate-passing app that fakes refusals by hiding controls is caught by mandatory replays (functional/prompt.md:23) and positive controls, and an app without live updates loses ~16% of functional and 50% of polish. Conforming app that could get all-or-nothing: a fully conforming, golden-quality app whose functional judge session exceeds the 9000 s judge timeout or the 11100 s scored budget gets reward 0 (test.sh:224-225), or loses late-protocol rows as 'NOT EXERCISED' binary0, so a strong and a mediocre app could both score 0 or be ordered by judge speed. Unmeasured, not observed.
suggested_fix: Before clearance, produce the REVIEW_POLICY-required hash-bound reward-discrimination record. Run full configured judge runs (frozen test.sh, claude-code with the task.toml judge) on the golden and on two or three mutated partial apps (for example no live push; no undo; no server-side permission checks), showing distinct, ordered rewards and no suite timeout. If the functional run overruns, reduce protocol workload, or get a recorded, authorized timeout change under five hours, rather than editing template scoring.
